nodes.label: Infrared Thermography Panel of Broiler Chickens
nodes.rationale: Research figure arranged as a 4-row x 5-column matrix over five birds/sessions: row A whole-body thermograms with a global temperature reading (36.8, 35.8, 36.5, 29.1, 31.9 C) and a scale bar, row B the matching RGB photographs with a coloured ROI box, row C the cropped thermal ROI with Avg/High/Low statistics, row D the same ROI rendered as a segmented/contoured false-colour map. It demonstrates the pipeline from raw thermogram to region-level temperature statistics.

nodes.label: Thermal Region-of-Interest Extraction
nodes.source_location: rows B and C, coloured bounding boxes
nodes.rationale: A bounding box is drawn on the visible-light frame and transferred to the co-registered thermogram, so temperature is read from a defined body region rather than from the whole frame including litter and equipment.

nodes.label: Avg/High/Low Surface Temperature Statistics
nodes.source_location: captions under rows C and D
nodes.rationale: Reducing an ROI to average, maximum and minimum temperature gives a compact, comparable feature vector; the spread between high and low is itself a thermoregulation cue. Reported values range roughly 25.8-40.9 C across the five subjects.

nodes.label: Paired RGB and Thermal Image Registration
nodes.rationale: RGB gives the semantics (which pixels are bird) and the thermal channel gives the measurement; pairing them is what makes automated, repeatable body-region thermometry possible.

nodes.label: Segmented False-Colour Thermal Map
nodes.rationale: Row D shows contour/point-cloud style segmentation over the ROI, isolating the hot core (comb, wattle, featherless skin) from cooler feathered areas. Exact segmentation algorithm is not stated in the figure.

edges.source_location: row C ROI to its Avg/High/Low caption
non-invasive thermal proxy for invasive physiological stress markers
